text: Definition 1 (Bellman violation-probability table) . For a fixed certificate horizon $H$ , policy $\pi$ , constraint $i$ , and transition kernel $P$ , define $q^{\pi}_{P,i}(s,b,h)$ as the conditional probability that the $i$ -th rounded budget coordinate becomes negative by the certificate horizon, when the rounded process starts from original state $s$ , rounded remaining-budget vector $b$ , and time index $h$ .

Definition 2 (Pessimistic Bellman distributional certificate) . Fix a policy $\pi\in\Pi_{H,\eta}$ , an empirical transition kernel $\widehat{P}$ , and row-wise confidence sets $\{\mathcal{C}_{s,a}\}_{s,a}$ . For each constraint $i$ , define the empirical violation table $\overline{q}_{i}^{\pi}(s,b,h)$ backward by $\overline{q}_{i}^{\pi}(s,b,H)=\mathbb{I}\{b_{i}<0\},$ and for $h=H-1,\ldots,0$ by $\overline{q}_{i}^{\pi}(s,b,h)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal{C}_{s,a}}p^{\top}\overline{q}_{i}^{\pi}(\cdot,B_{h}(s,a,b),h+1),\qquad a=\pi_{h}(s,b),$ (7) The pessimistic Bellman distributional certificate of $\pi$ is $\overline{q}_{i,H,\eta}(\pi)=\sum\nolimits_{s}\mu(s)\overline{q}_{i}^{\pi}(s,b^{0},0)$ for all $i\in[m].$

Proposition 1 (Certified safety, Proof in Appendix D ) . With high probability over the shared row samples, simultaneously for every $\pi\in\Pi_{H,\eta}$ , $\overline{q}_{i,H,\eta}(\pi)\leq\delta_{i}$ for every $i\in[m]$ implies that $\pi$ is feasible for the original infinite-horizon chance-constrained MDP.

Definition 3 ( $\xi$ -optimal finite certified solver) . For $\xi\geq 0$ , whenever the certified feasible set is nonempty, a finite certified solver returns a policy $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi_{\mathcal{O}}$ and its Bellman reward and safety tables such that $\overline{q}_{i,H_{\alpha},\eta}(\widehat{\pi})\leq\delta_{i}$ for all $i\in[m]$ and $\widehat{J}(\widehat{\pi})\geq\max\nolimits_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathcal{O}}:\ \overline{q}_{i,H_{\alpha},\eta}(\pi)\leq\delta_{i},\ i\in[m]}\widehat{J}(\pi)-\xi.$ (11) When $\xi=0$ , the solver is exact.

Assumption 1 (Bounded successor support and certified planning) . There is a known integer $d_{0}\geq 2$ , independent of $|\mathcal{S}|$ , $|\mathcal{A}|$ , $\gamma$ , $\varepsilon$ , and $\rho$ , such that $|\operatorname{supp}P(\cdot\mid s,a)|\leq d_{0},\qquad(s,a)\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}.$ (12) The finite policy class $\Pi_{\mathcal{O}}\subseteq\Pi_{H,\eta}$ is fixed before sampling. Whenever the tightened problem is feasible, the certified planner returns an $\xi$ -optimal policy in the sense of Definition 3 .

Theorem 1 (Bellman-certified upper bound) . There are universal constants $C,c>0$ such that the following holds. Fix $\zeta\in(0,1)$ , $\rho\in(0,1]$ , $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ , and $\xi\geq 0$ , and assume the set defining $V_{\rho}^{\star}$ is nonempty. Suppose Algorithm 1 uses a solver satisfying Assumption 1 , with fixed support bound $d_{0}$ . Run it with $\alpha_{\rm tail}=\eta_{i}=\bar{\eta}_{\varepsilon}$ for every constraint and $n=\lfloor D/(|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|)\rfloor$ samples per row. If the total generative-model transition-sample budget $D$ satisfies $D\geq Cd_{0}|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|\left(\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)^{3}\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)\rho^{2}}\right)\log^{c}\!\left(\frac{8d_{0}|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|}{\zeta\varepsilon\rho(1-\gamma)}\right).$ (14) Then with probability at least $1-\zeta$ , Algorithm 1 returns a policy $\widehat{\pi}$ satisfying $q_{P,i}(\widehat{\pi})\leq\delta_{i}$ for every $i\in[m]$ and $J_{P}(\widehat{\pi})\geq V_{\rho}^{\star}-\varepsilon-\xi$ .

Theorem 2 (Model-based CCMDP lower bound) . There are universal constants $c,c_{0}>0$ such that the following holds for every fixed $d_{0}\geq 2$ , $\gamma\in[1/2,1)$ , $\varepsilon\in(0,c_{0}/(1-\gamma))$ , $\rho\in(0,c_{0})$ , $|\mathcal{S}|\geq 4$ , and $|\mathcal{A}|\geq 2$ . Use $\alpha_{\rm tail}=\eta=\bar{\eta}_{\varepsilon}$ and take $\Pi_{\mathcal{O}}=\Pi_{H,\eta}$ in ( 13 ). Let $\Pi_{\mathrm{det}}$ be the full deterministic policy class represented by the trajectory parameters in Section 2 . Any generative-model learner that, on every one-constraint CCMDP satisfying $|\operatorname{supp}P(\cdot\mid s,a)|\leq d_{0}$ and having a nonempty rounded $\rho$ -interior feasible set, returns with probability at least $2/3$ a policy $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi_{\mathrm{det}}$ satisfying jointly $q_{P}(\widehat{\pi})\leq\delta$ and $J_{P}(\widehat{\pi})\geq V^{\star}_{\rho}-\varepsilon$ must, in the worst case, use a total number $D$ of transition samples satisfying $D\geq c|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|\left(\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)^{3}\varepsilon^{2}}+{\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)\rho^{2}}}\right).$ (15)

Assumption 2 (Local regularity) . We assume the local smoothness, bounded-score, bounded-variance, compact-interior-iterate, feasible-initialization, and bounded-multiplier conditions used by the trajectory oracles and variance-reduced updates [ 50 , 51 , 29 ] . The complete proof-level optimization conditions are stated in Assumption 3 . In particular, that assumption includes the additional residual-domination condition ( 35 ).

Theorem 3 (Model-free trajectory certificate) . There is a universal constant $C_{\rm pg}>0$ such that the following holds. Fix $\alpha_{\rm tail}\in(0,(1-\gamma)^{-1})$ , grid widths $\eta_{i}>0$ , margin $\rho\in(0,1]$ , KKT accuracy $\varepsilon_{\rm kkt}\in(0,1)$ , and confidence $\zeta\in(0,1)$ . Run Algorithm 2 with $H=\left\lceil\log(1/((1-\gamma)\alpha_{\rm tail}))/(1-\gamma)\right\rceil$ , and use $M_{\rm val}=\left\lceil 2\log(2m/\zeta)/\rho^{2}\right\rceil$ fresh validation trajectories per constraint. Let $K_{\rm opt}$ denote the resulting problem-dependent local optimization constant. Under Assumptions 2 and 3 , it suffices that the expected total number $D:=\mathbb{E}[N_{\rm trans}]$ of environment transitions for optimization and validation satisfies $\displaystyle D\geq$ $\displaystyle\frac{C_{\rm pg}K_{\rm opt}G^{2}m}{\varepsilon_{\rm kkt}^{3}(1-\gamma)^{3}}\log^{3}\left(\frac{2}{(1-\gamma)\alpha_{\rm tail}}\right)\log^{4}\left(\frac{8K_{\rm opt}G^{2}m}{\varepsilon_{\rm kkt}\rho\zeta(1-\gamma)^{3}\alpha_{\rm tail}}\right)$ (17) $\displaystyle+\frac{C_{\rm pg}m}{\rho^{2}(1-\gamma)}\log\left(\frac{2}{(1-\gamma)\alpha_{\rm tail}}\right)\log\left(\frac{2m}{\zeta}\right).$ Then the optimization phase returns a candidate satisfying $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{H}(\theta_{\rm cand})]\leq\varepsilon_{\rm kkt}$ . Moreover, with probability at least $1-\zeta$ over the independent validation trajectories, Algorithm 2 either returns validation unresolved or accepts a policy feasible for the original infinite-horizon CCMDP. On the same event, if the returned candidate satisfies $q^{H}_{P,i}(\theta_{\rm cand})\leq\delta_{i}-\rho$ for all $i$ , then it is accepted.

Proposition 2 (Hardness of exact deterministic planning) . Even when the transition model is known and deterministic, exact reward maximization over deterministic policies subject to a discounted chance constraint is $\mathsf{NP-hard}$ .
